guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
The opposite trap is forced adulthood: perfect discipline, no visible needs, and very little joy or closeness. In that case the next adult act may be asking for help, expressing a preference, or letting a safe person see something imperfect—not tightening control again. Judge the strategy as well as the need. Wanting closeness is legitimate; demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space is not the same thing. The Guide helps find a workable way to meet the need without erasing either person.
brief:
- the opposite trap is forced adulthood: perfect discipline, no visible needs, and very little joy or closeness (the three signs together)
- in that case (keep the scope: this is for someone stuck in forced adulthood), the next adult act may be asking for help, saying what you'd prefer, or letting a safe person see something imperfect, not tightening control again (keep "may", the "or" list and "safe person")
- judge the strategy as well as the need (keep "as well as": the need isn't judged away)
- wanting closeness is legitimate; demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space isn't the same thing
- the Guide helps find a workable way to meet the need without erasing either person (keep both people)
- context, not for the text: When to Change the Strategy already has "texting a friend that you're having a rough day instead of saying you're fine", and Also Look Outward has "reaching toward people is part of taking care of your little one too", so the imperfect-showing and the closeness points stay short.
note: Turn 56 (2026-10-15): The Inner Guide Comes Later, group 3 (P3 of the h1), brief from the dedup and stance ledger (experiments/t56-guide/).
